items.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002
items.q: Plus I was a Fred Astaire freak. So I’d walk two miles, scrub a woman’s floor, walk two miles from the money she gave me and go see Fred Astaire in South Fork, Pennsylvania, just so I could try to learn those songs.

ctx.x: Was there music in your grandparents’ house?

Well you know as a little kid I used to do a lot of improvising because my grandmother was a beautiful singer and she played the piano. And my great grandfather, who was from the Native American, was a wonderful painter but they said he had a wonderful singing voice. And of course my grandfather when he got drunk, which was most of the time, loved to sing. But he wasn’t that good. But my grandmother was very good. But what I did as a kid, I used to sing just like — kind of like improvising like on Native American…
Wow. That was a nice little bridge there between those two things.
